item.content:encoded:
By this logic, every piece of Foundation fiction takes place in your protagonist's imagination.

That can be arguable. IRL, Moto42 wrote about SCP-173, but it was an assortment of other people who wrote about Foundation fiction (who moved from passive consumers of SCP-173 to active agents who produce and remix the content). Unless we are all manifestations of Moto42.

Now that I think about it, for all the times the Foundation is written to recognise its own fictional nature as a narrative, not a lot is done about the Foundation being someone's figment of imagination (aside from that SCP that imply the Foundation-verse is just the SCP's massive delusion).

item.content:encoded:
There was a show (soap opera?) that ended with the plot twist that the entire show took place inside a kid's imagination. Closing shot of the show was a zoom out from the protagonist's house and it revealed that the house was inside the kid's snowglobe.

Because this was the '90s, this show had crossover episodes with a bunch of other shows. Each of those, in turn, had their own crossovers. This lead to the joke that all fictional television took place in the kid's snowglobe.

By this logic, every piece of Foundation fiction takes place in your protagonist's imagination.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Yes, I like this. I think the narrative is a bit bare-bones, as if I have it correctly it's really just a small segment of 173's existence as he moves between containment facilities, but there's some really rich and moving imagery here. I did not think to consider 173 an empathetic character, which, oddly enough, seems to be what more than a few of these entries are going for, but it works here alongside the theme of boxes and attention and such. His diction also lends itself to that end, being very limited and practical in scope, and his perception of the world and how he perceives time feel rather novel, as he is literally just a statue and it's hard to imagine keeping a mental pocketwatch.

+1. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8xVfjkb-xVs

item.title: Thanks, Attribution, and Other Matters
item.content:encoded:
This is my entry for the 173fest not-contest. Allow me to express thanks to MaliceAforethought, Icepick (Mortos), SunnyClockwork, 9Volt, Flawed, and jishwa for reading it.

Obviously, this Tale features SCP-173 (The Sculpture) by Moto42

+ show block
– hide block

Premise: The situation described in the article 'SCP-173' is the imagination/fantasy of a sculpture.

Moving Ones: Mostly humans (defined by being able to move)
Unmoving Ones: Other artwork (sculptures and paintings), which the narrator imagines to be kept in their own walled enclosures (i.e. containment)
Cycles: A passage of time defined by the appearance of the Moving Ones from the narrator's POV
